rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed yet, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple unimodal baseline is competitive and what reference performance to use for later comparisons. config_001 tests a minimal RNA-only, single-profile model with a standard PCA representation. It is the best next experiment because it establishes a low-risk baseline for RNA modeling and creates a reference point for evaluating RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion without prematurely spending budget on more complex configurations.

Only the RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline has been tested, so it is still unknown whether image features carry useful predictive signal. config_010 tests an image-only, single-profile ResNet-50 model, providing a direct modality baseline while keeping the profile setting simple. This is the best next experiment because it isolates the importance of the image modality before investing in more complex multimodal fusion, aggregation, or encoder choices.

The only strong signal so far is RNA-only PCA singleprofile, which substantially outperforms image-only ResNet in both accuracy and F1. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve this promising RNA baseline without changing the representation. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and modality, testing only the shift to multiprofile with average pooling. This is a low-confound, efficient next step: it exploits the current best direction while clarifying whether profile aggregation is worth further investment before testing more complex encoders, transformers, or multimodal fusion.

The strongest completed result is config_002: RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool aggregation, which substantially outperforms RNA-only singleprofile and far exceeds image-only ResNet50. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool for the same multiprofile RNA representation. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and pca_n2000 fixed, so it cleanly isolates the aggregation effect. This is a high-value next experiment because it exploits the current best direction while reducing uncertainty about an important design choice before spending budget on more complex multimodal or new encoder variants.

RNA PCA with multiprofile avgpool is currently the strongest setting (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), while image-only ResNet with a single profile is weak (accuracy 0.208). It is unclear whether the image modality is intrinsically weak or whether multiprofile avgpool aggregation, which helped RNA, can improve image performance. config_011 tests image ResNet with multiprofile avgpool, changing only profile/aggregation relative to config_010 and providing a same-profile image baseline for later fusion comparisons. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about whether image features are worth adding before spending limited budget on more complex multimodal fusion or other encoders.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile + avgpool is much better than singleprofile or transformer aggregation for both RNA and image models, with RNA-only PCA multiprofile avgpool reaching 0.5907 accuracy. The key remaining uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion can improve over the strong RNA-only baseline when the same profile, aggregation, and tested encoders are held fixed. config_018 keeps PCA, ResNet50, multiprofile, and avgpool constant and only adds concat fusion, allowing a direct comparison against config_002 and config_011. This is the cleanest next test of whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing before spending budget on stronger encoders or more complex fusion variants.

The strongest result so far is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet, avgpool, concat) with validation accuracy 0.6186, modestly above the best RNA-only multiprofile avgpool result (0.5907). This suggests the current multimodal setup is promising, but it is unclear whether concat is the best fusion rule, especially since image-only performance is weak. config_019 changes only the fusion method to weighted while keeping the same model, profile, encoders, and aggregation, so it directly tests whether weighted fusion can improve on the current best configuration. This is the best next use of a limited experiment because it exploits the strongest evidence, isolates one important design choice, and has a high expected performance ceiling.

The best completed run is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet, avgpool, weighted) with 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1, and avgpool has already outperformed transformer in RNA-only multiprofile. The remaining uncertainty in this promising family is whether transformer aggregation can improve the multimodal setting. config_021 changes only aggregation relative to config_019, isolating that effect while exploiting the current best profile, encoder, and fusion choices, making it a low-risk and informative next experiment under a limited budget.

Existing evidence shows the best current setup is multimodal multiprofile with PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion (accuracy 0.639, F1 0.620), while RNA-only multiprofile avgpool reaches 0.591 and image-only ResNet50 is much weaker. The key uncertainty is whether the image representation is limiting the multimodal gain, since ResNet50 performs poorly as an image-only model. This experiment tests that directly by replacing ResNet50 with imagenet_vit_l while keeping the otherwise best-known settings fixed: PCA RNA encoder, multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It is the best next experiment because it is a clean one-factor extension of the current best configuration, isolates the effect of image representation, and can either improve performance or clarify whether image features are the bottleneck without confounding changes to profile, aggregation, or fusion.

The strongest evidence is that multimodal multiprofile models with weighted fusion and avgpool aggregation perform best, especially config_019 with PCA and ResNet50, while config_025 shows the image-encoder difference is small. The major untested factor in this promising region is the RNA representation. config_031 tests scvi_n200 while holding the other strong settings fixed, directly clarifying whether a learned RNA encoder improves on PCA in the best-performing multimodal setup. This is an efficient exploitation of the current evidence while reducing uncertainty about an important design choice.
